tolerance.note: pass if |got-expected| <= rel*|expected| (abs when expected is 0); integers, booleans, strings, nulls, regimes and error objects exact (contract 1e-6 / 1e-9)

calc_module: lib/sims/families/optics.calc.js (global FITCalcOptics, API_VERSION 1); each case calls FITCalcOptics.<op>(input)
convention: Angles in degrees, measured from the NORMAL; lengths in cm unless the field name says otherwise; refractive indices n >= 1 (n < 1 -> ConstraintViolation refractive_index_below_1, checked first); angle of incidence 0 <= theta <= 90 inclusive (else ConstraintViolation angle_out_of_range_0_90). THIN-LENS SIGN CONVENTION: REAL-IS-POSITIVE (per the contract): f > 0 converging, f < 0 diverging; u > 0 real object; v > 0 real image, v < 0 virtual; 1/f = 1/u + 1/v; m = -v/u (m < 0 inverted). Lensmaker radii use the CARTESIAN convention (R > 0 when the centre of curvature is on the outgoing side; flat face R = null), 1/f = (n_lens/n_medium - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2), f returned in the real-is-positive sense. P in dioptres = 1/f with f in metres. Speed of light c = 3.00e8 m/s. Two lenses: u2 = d - v1 (may be negative: virtual object), m_total = m1 m2. Telescope: normal adjustment, M = -f_obj/f_eye (negative = inverted image). Microscope: standard approximation M = -(L/f_obj)(D/f_eye). Magnifier and microscope near point D default to 25 cm (ruling 19:41). TIR test (ruling 19:41): TIR iff n1 sin(theta1) - n2 > 1e-9 (absolute), so theta1 = C is not TIR. two_lens with u = f1 (within 1e-9) -> RESULT {v1_cm: null, u2_cm: null, v2_cm: f2_cm, m_total: null, at_infinity: true}; all other two_lens results carry at_infinity: false. Regimes are RESULTS (rulings 16:44, 17:46, 19:31): TIR -> {refraction_deg: null, tir: true, critical_deg}; incidence exactly at C -> refraction_deg 90, tir false; object at F -> {v_cm, m, real, upright: null, at_infinity: true}. Errors (17:46): schema classes only, contract reason codes in expected.reason, error object = error/reason only. 'level' (1-5, see 'levels') is an informational tag.
oracle: Hand formulas from Hecht, Optics; Young and Freedman, University Physics; Pedrotti, Introduction to Optics. Recomputed in _build_optics_kats.py by (A) plain-float textbook formulas and (B) 40-digit mpmath with different formulations (vector Snell, Newtonian x x' = f^2, ABCD ray-transfer matrices, surface-power lensmaker); never the module under test.

cases.hand_check: theta_r = theta_i = 30 deg (angles from the normal). Hecht, Optics (5th ed.), law of reflection.
Boundary 0 deg: theta_r = 0. Hecht, Optics (5th ed.).
0 <= theta <= 90 is inclusive, so 90 is valid: theta_r = 90. Hecht, Optics (5th ed.).
95 > 90 violates the shared 0-90 convention -> ConstraintViolation, reason angle_out_of_range_0_90 (contract code).
-10 < 0 -> ConstraintViolation, reason angle_out_of_range_0_90.
sin r = 1.0 sin30/1.5 = 1/3; r = 19.4712 deg. n1 <= n2 so critical_deg null, tir false. Hecht, Optics (5th ed.), Snell's law.
sin r = sin45/1.33 = 0.531659; r = 32.1176 deg. Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.), refraction.

cases.desc: Glass to air below the critical angle, 30 deg
cases.hand_check: sin r = 1.5 sin30 = 0.75; r = 48.5904 deg; C = asin(1/1.5) = 41.8103 deg reported because n1 > n2. Hecht, Optics (5th ed.).
sin r = 0 -> r = 0. Hecht, Optics (5th ed.).

cases.desc: Refractive index from i and r (light from air)
cases.hand_check: n = sin40/sin25 = 0.642788/0.422618 = 1.52097. Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.).
sin0/sin0 = 0/0 is indeterminate -> MathError, reason indeterminate_normal_incidence (contract code).
sin30/sin0 = 0.5/0 -> MathError, reason division_by_zero (contract code).
v = c/n = 3.00e8/1.5 = 2.00e8 m/s (contract fixes c = 3.00e8 m/s). Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.).
n1 = 0.9 < 1 -> ConstraintViolation, reason refractive_index_below_1 (contract code).
sin C = n2/n1 = 2/3; C = 41.8103 deg. Hecht, Optics (5th ed.), total internal reflection.
sin C = 1.33/1.5 = 0.886667; C = 62.4573 deg. Pedrotti, Pedrotti and Pedrotti, Introduction to Optics.

cases.desc: No critical angle when n1 < n2
cases.hand_check: sin C = 1.5 > 1 has no solution -> MathError, reason no_critical_angle (contract code).

cases.desc: TIR at 60 deg, glass to air (regime result)
cases.hand_check: 1.5 sin60 = 1.299 > 1 and 60 > C: total internal reflection is a RESULT (rulings 16:44/19:31 pattern), refraction_deg null, tir true. Hecht, Optics (5th ed.).

cases.desc: Incidence exactly at the critical angle (n1 = 2, C = 30 deg)
cases.hand_check: sin C = 1/2, C = 30 deg exactly; contract: theta1 = C gives refraction_deg 90, tir false. In binary floats 2 sin30 = 0.9999999999999999, so asin gives 89.9999991 deg (rel 9e-9, inside 1e-6); a module must not flag TIR from a 1-ulp difference.

cases.desc: Grazing 90 deg from glass to air is TIR
cases.hand_check: 90 > C = 41.81 deg -> TIR regime result. Hecht, Optics (5th ed.).
sin r = 2.42 sin20 = 0.827693; r = 55.8620 deg; C = asin(1/2.42) = 24.4075 deg. Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.).
1/v = 1/10 - 1/30 = 1/15 -> v = 15 cm (real); m = -v/u = -0.5 (inverted, diminished). Real-is-positive. Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.), thin lenses.
1/v = 1/10 - 1/20 = 1/20 -> v = 20 cm; m = -1 (same size, inverted). Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.).
1/v = 1/10 - 1/5 = -1/10 -> v = -10 cm (virtual); m = -(-10)/5 = +2 (upright, magnified). Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.).
1/v = -1/10 - 1/20 = -3/20 -> v = -6.6667 cm (virtual); m = +1/3 (upright, diminished). Hecht, Optics (5th ed.).

cases.desc: Object at the focal point (regime result)
cases.hand_check: u = f: 1/v = 0, image at infinity. Contract makes this a RESULT (at_infinity true, other fields null), not MathError.
u <= 0 -> ConstraintViolation, reason object_distance_not_positive (contract code).
1/f with f = 0 is undefined -> MathError, reason zero_focal_length (contract code).

cases.desc: Power of a 50 cm converging lens
cases.hand_check: P = 1/(0.50 m) = +2.0 D. Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.).

cases.desc: Power of a -25 cm diverging lens
cases.hand_check: P = 1/(-0.25 m) = -4.0 D. Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.).
1/f = (1.5-1)(1/20 + 1/20) = 0.05 -> f = 20 cm, P = 5 D. Cartesian radii (R2 < 0 for a biconvex lens). Hecht, Optics (5th ed.), lensmaker's formula.

cases.desc: Lensmaker: plano-convex, flat face R2 = null
cases.hand_check: Flat face: 1/R2 = 0; 1/f = 0.5/15 -> f = 30 cm, P = 3.333 D. Hecht, Optics (5th ed.).
1/f = 0.5(-1/20 - 1/20) = -0.05 -> f = -20 cm (diverging). Hecht, Optics (5th ed.).

cases.desc: Layered media: same glass lens immersed in water
cases.hand_check: 1/f = (1.5/1.33 - 1)(0.1) = 0.0127820 -> f = 78.235 cm, P = 1.2782 D (vs 20 cm in air). Pedrotti, Pedrotti and Pedrotti, Introduction to Optics, lens in a medium.

cases.desc: Lensmaker: lens index equals medium index
cases.hand_check: Bracket (n_lens/n_medium - 1) = 0 -> 1/f = 0 -> MathError, reason infinite_focal_length (contract code).
v1 = 20; u2 = 40 - 20 = 20; 1/v2 = 1/15 - 1/20 -> v2 = 60; m = (-20/20)(-60/20) = 3. Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.), lens combinations.

cases.desc: Two lenses: virtual object for the second lens (u2 < 0)

cases.hand_check: M = D/f = 5 (relaxed eye); M = 1 + D/f = 6 (image at near point). Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.), the magnifier.

cases.desc: Simple magnifier, near point omitted (default 25 cm)
cases.hand_check: D defaults to 25 cm when near_point_cm is omitted: 25/10 = 2.5, 1 + 2.5 = 3.5.
M = -f_obj/f_eye = -20 (inverted); length = 100 + 5 = 105 cm. Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.), telescopes.
M = -(L/f_obj)(D/f_eye) = -(16/1)(25/2.5) = -160. Young and Freedman, University Physics (15th ed.), microscopes.

cases.desc: Two lenses: object at lens 1's focus, v1 at infinity (regime result)
cases.hand_check: u = f1 (within 1e-9) -> v1 = infinity; parallel rays reach lens 2 and focus at v2 = f2 = 15 cm, independent of d. Ruling 19:41: RESULT {v1_cm, u2_cm, m_total: null, v2_cm: f2_cm, at_infinity: true}, not an error. Hecht, Optics (5th ed.).

cases.desc: Two lenses: object at lens 1's focus, diverging second lens
cases.hand_check: u = f1 -> collimated beam into a diverging lens: virtual image at v2 = f2 = -10 cm (ruling 19:41 regime result).

cases.desc: Compound microscope, near point omitted (default 25 cm)
cases.hand_check: Ruling 19:41: near_point_cm defaults to 25 cm. M = -(16/0.5)(25/2.5) = -(32)(10) = -320.
